title: SEAM: Shot Entity-Attribute Memory for Consistent Short-Drama Generation at Scale
abstract: arXiv:2608.22725v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Short-drama generation has grown into a large, industrialized pipeline, and as it scales from isolated shots to the episode level, visual continuity has become a critical bottleneck. Current agent frameworks generate each shot in isolation, so context drifts across shots and props, character posture, and blocking turn inconsistent. Once assembled, these small discrepancies amplify into severe visual breaks. We present SEAM (Shot Entity-Attribute Memory), a training-free, model-agnostic memory graph that repairs continuity entirely at the prompt-text layer by extracting a multi-dimensional state for every shot, retrieving only causally prior context over the resulting graph, filtering it selectively, and injecting the surviving constraints by natural-language prompt rewriting. translated_title: SEAM：用于大规模短剧一致生成的镜头实体-属性记忆
translated_abstract: 短剧生成已发展成一个庞大且工业化的流水线，随着其从孤立镜头扩展到剧集级别，视觉连续性已成为关键瓶颈。当前的智能体框架孤立地生成每个镜头，导致跨镜头的上下文漂移，使得道具、角色姿态和构图变得不一致。一旦组装起来，这些小差异会放大为严重的视觉断裂。我们提出了SEAM（镜头实体-属性记忆），一种无需训练、模型无关的记忆图，它通过在提示文本层修复连续性：提取每个镜头的多维状态，在生成的图上仅检索因果先前的上下文，选择性过滤，并通过自然语言提示重写注入剩余的约束。我们进一步发布了SEAM-Bench，一个双盲连续性故事板基准，在该基准上，SEAM将跨剧集连续性召回率从0.700提升到0.946，并具有泛化性。
tldr: SEAM通过构建无需训练的模型无关记忆图，在提示文本层修复短剧生成中的视觉连续性，显著提升跨剧集一致性。
en_tdlr: SEAM repairs visual continuity in short-drama generation by building a training-free, model-agnostic memory graph at the prompt-text layer, significantly boosting cross-episode consistency.
